item.title: Video of dolphin carrying its dead newborn through the Indian Ocean reveals a deep and old 'mourning ritual'
item.description: Fraggle, a grieving mother dolphin, carried her deceased calf for six days, a poignant testament to her profound maternal love. Captured by drone footage in the Indian Ocean, this heart-wrenching scene revealed the support of her pod, which gathered around her in solidarity during her mourning. This behavior, seen in over twenty cetacean species, underscores their intricate social connections and possible awareness of mortality.

item.title: Florida's first flesh-eating bacteria death of 2026
item.description: Florida health officials confirmed the state's first 2026 Vibrio vulnificus fatality. This flesh-eating bacteria thrives in warm coastal waters during summer months. Individuals with weakened immune systems face significantly higher risks. Public awareness is crucial as cases double during the peak season.

item.title: US moves closer to deep-sea mining near American Samoa with 31.5 million acre lease plan
item.description: The United States has moved a step closer to deep-sea mining after the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) proposed auctioning two massive seabed lease areas near American Samoa for mineral exploration. The proposal marks a significant milestone in the country's efforts to secure critical mineral supplies for clean energy, electronics and national security.

item.title: Colombia intercepted a boat near the Malpelo sanctuary carrying 1,764 pounds of marine animals
item.description: Colombian authorities have intercepted a fishing vessel carrying approximately 1,764 pounds of suspected illegally caught marine animals believed to have been taken from the protected Malpelo Fauna and Flora Sanctuary, bringing renewed attention to illegal fishing in one of the country's most ecologically important marine reserves.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Man reunited with lost wedding ring after 10 years as 9-year-old niece finds it in Minnesota lake
item.description: A Minnesota man has been reunited with his wedding ring nearly a decade after losing it at the bottom of a lake, thanks to an unexpected discovery by his 9-year-old niece during a family vacation. Stephen Meyer lost his wedding ring in 2016 while swimming with his son in Lake Belle Taine, where his family owns a cabin.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 60 venomous snakes, cocaine, guns and 22,000 dollars in cash seized during New Mexico drug raid
item.description: Federal agents investigating an alleged cocaine trafficking operation in New Mexico made a shocking discovery after uncovering 60 snakes, half a pound of cocaine, three firearms and 22,000 dollars in cash during a raid on a home in the South Valley area near Albuquerque. The seizure inventory included cobras, mambas, pit vipers and pythons, along with an inland taipan, widely regarded as one of the world's most venomous snakes.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Long history of unlawful violence': Global watchdogs condemn Pakistan's crackdown in PoK
item.description: International oversight bodies are sounding the alarm over growing violence and restrictions on media freedom during elections. Amnesty International has documented harsh actions against protesters in PoK's Rawalakot, and the Committee to Protect Journalists has identified worsening conditions for reporters. Alarmingly, two independent journalists are reportedly missing after being abducted from their office, with the protest movement accounting for more than eighty fatalities.

item.title: Parody Quotes Spur Debate: X screenshots of Clavicular go viral; fans split over his influence
item.description: A parody account on X went viral after sharing quotes attributed to Clavicular, claiming he believes he is among the world's most influential people and on a "once in a generation" rise. The post also included ambitious remarks about changing culture and even ruling beyond the planet. While the account is clearly labelled as parody, the viral image sparked widespread debate over Clavicular's confidence and growing online influence.

item.title: Asmongold Slams Candace Owens: streamer says she’s ‘totally cooked’; viral clip fuels backlash debate
item.description: Asmongold strongly criticised Candace Owens over her Charlie Kirk conspiracy claims, arguing she has severely damaged her credibility and alienated mainstream audiences. He claimed there was little chance of repairing her public image and suggested her remaining supporters would continue demanding more extreme claims. His remarks, shared widely on social media, sparked fresh debate, with users divided between supporting his criticism and defending Owens.

item.title: Quote by Ludwig Wittgenstein: 'The real question of life after death isn't whether or not it exists...'
item.description: Philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein challenged the preoccupation with life after death, suggesting that eternal existence does not address the fundamental questions of life’s meaning. His reflections emerged amidst the chaos of World War One. In contemporary discussions on digital immortality, this crucial insight often gets overshadowed; authentic meaning resides in fully embracing the present and living with intention.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Quote of the day by JS Mill: 'I have learned to seek my happiness by limiting my desires...'
item.description: Victorian philosopher John Stuart Mill believed that true happiness lies in limiting our desires rather than endlessly pursuing them. After facing a mental crisis due to his upbringing, Mill shifted his philosophy, warning that unending desire leads to a hedonic treadmill. Today, our consumer-driven culture reflects this endless chase; by curbing material wishes, we can unlock a wealth of inner fulfillment and deeper contentment.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Man rejects Rs 2 crore offer in India and chooses $160K in the US because...
In 1974, Spain imported two tons of American red crayfish for aquaculture; 50 years later...
item.description: Fifty years ago, American red crayfish were introduced to Spain's Guadalquivir River basin, and they have since established a permanent presence. These aggressive invaders have wreaked havoc on local wildlife and disrupted aquatic ecosystems. Yet, local communities have successfully built an economy around their harvesting and processing. This dependence has sparked legal disputes, resulting in a compromise that permits regulated harvesting, balancing ecological health with economic viability.
